goalReview.goalStandard:
## Goal-aligned decisions

The [sequence](../planning/sequence.md) and selected work order determine
current placement and authority. The mission is the outcome; the critical path
is the dependency route to the next outcome. Useful prerequisite or
risk-reduction work must name the blocked outcome it enables. Process activity,
receipt volume and agent utilization are not progress by themselves. Goal
alignment grants no authority to reorder or expand work. In all phases, the Goal
Alignment and Process Cost procedure lives in the generated role skills
[WO-043, 2026-09-11].

Accuracy takes priority over agreement in every phase. The already-equipped
Correctness over Sycophancy rule applies to operator suggestions and the agent's
own premises equally: challenge unsupported claims, distinguish observation
from inference, state material uncertainty, and correct mistakes when evidence
changes. A confident request or an earlier decision is not proof of correctness.
Record material disagreement and its evidence in the same decision or phase
receipt; do not manufacture dissent or seek approval for ordinary judgment.

| Lens                                  | Decision question                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Policy resistance / fixes that fail   | Will local goals or guards undo one another?                                                              |
| Tragedy of the commons                | Does the solution consume shared compute, context or operator attention without accounting for the total? |
| Drift to low performance              | Does it improve an explicit outcome standard rather than normalize a worse baseline?                      |
| Escalation                            | Will additional process provoke more process or workarounds?                                              |
| Success to the successful             | Are credible alternatives excluded merely because the current mechanism already has investment?           |
| Shifting the burden to the intervenor | Does the solution remove recurring operator rescue or depend on it?                                       |
| Rule beating                          | Can the evidence pass without the intended behavior occurring?                                            |
| Seeking the wrong goal                | Does it advance operator flow and the selected product outcome rather than a proxy?                       |

Naive Interventionism adds the existing system's useful functions, affected
consumers, second-order harm, reversibility and smallest useful probe. NoOp
records what happens if nothing changes, why action or inaction wins, and the
evidence that would reopen the choice. Scale detail to consequence: explain
applicable risks and briefly group immaterial lenses with a reason; do not
manufacture eight repetitive paragraphs for routine edits.

Record evidence of benefit and the risks of intervening in existing behavior;
verification and handoff compare observed outcomes with the promised benefit.
Required legal or release actions retain their existing authority; NoOp is a
considered alternative, not an ambient veto or permission to abandon authorized
work.



Material choices and rationales go in existing phase evidence: per-order
`docs/evidence/WO-NNN/decisions.md` and cited product sections for work-order
decisions; planning dispositions/candidate records for planning choices; the
independent report or refutation receipt for its judgment; retained closeout
evidence for release decisions. The decisions index exposes per-order records.
Reuse and link a current rationale until its assumptions change; do not create
a parallel decision log or an extra approval ritual.


This launchpad is the operator's own DotLn instance. Its purpose is to plan and
run bounded, evidence-gated work orders across the operator's repositories, so
that every change arrives as a pull request the operator reads before it merges,
while the kit itself stays upstream and reaches this fork only through starter
updates. The first workstream is DotLn-Angular, an Nx and Angular monorepo that
serves two outcomes at once: the operator's reference Angular workspace, which a
colleague should recognize as the way the operator builds Angular, and the
operator's sandbox app, one app with sub-apps behind a menu: a scene for
authoring game AI from a toolbox mined from the works the operator reads, a
view of DotLn's machinery where a change to an agent's mechanisms shows what
changes in an example use case, the operator's own digital twin, and side
utilities. Every new idea lives there first as a toy the operator plays with
before promoting the ones that work, for the five UIFA roles, people and
software actors alike. The app is not wired to DotLn core: its data comes from
public mining into its own store, served to the UI through its own API, and it
informs the platform through GitHub issues, never by writing a control record,
so that the app improves the platform, the platform the starter, the starter
this fork, and the fork the app in turn. The critical path runs from registering
that repository in this launchpad, through one witnessed target order that
scaffolds the workspace, to a foundation where a feature is added by convention:
shared libraries, the component taxonomy, events and stores, the sub-app shell,
and a legitimate client-side authentication and permission model. Later
workstreams join the same way: one registration and one planning pass each,
with the fork's own machinery changes cut as self orders beside them.

episode.statement: Plan refuter session statement: I read only the canonical refutation prompt at <tmp>/scratch/refute-prompt.json, in full and in parts, and one directory listing of that scratch directory; the listing showed other files there, and I opened none of them. I read no repository file, planning document, receipt, intake, web page or prior judgment. I used local python3 only to parse the prompt and to write and check my result against the prompt's resultSchema; I used no model tool. The only files I wrote are refutation-result.json and refutation-statement.txt in that scratch directory. I wrote no repository file and ran no Git command or subagent. orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: No critical path is declared: the goal review records 'unavailable: docs/planning/critical-path-2026-09-08.md; this instance has not declared a critical path'. Against the route the goal standard narrates (registration, one witnessed scaffold, then a foundation of shared libraries, the component taxonomy, events and stores, the sub-app shell and a client-side authentication and permission model), the only foundation element left in the sequence is WO-008, placed ninth, and WO-025 names neither it nor any other blocked outcome; it unblocks no product gate. Its value is risk reduction on the documents every session reads at start, plus one operator decision (whether the record of their directions is complete). NoOp in the records: the cost-table row for WO-025 has metrics: null, and the shifting-the-burden observation records corrections as unavailable for all five measured orders and directions of 1, 3, 6, 5 and 3 with no attribution to stale documents, so the records carry no measured cost of leaving the documents as they are. What inaction keeps is visible only in the order itself: a profile with a **Checked:** line in a shape the operator has chosen to replace, and facts not current to WO-015's merge and DotLn Angular v0.6.0. Action wins on the operator's chosen profile shape, not on measured cost. The choice reopens if the orders after it show no corrections or directions attributable to stale standing documents and no role uses the new profile shape.
orders.systemTraps: Policy resistance: criterion 4 requires the multisets of capture digests and dates in the operator record to be equal before and after, while the objective asks for each direction once, 'none narrated', in a scannable order; merging a duplicated citation changes the multiset, so the guard rewards keeping duplicates (finding on criterion:4). Tragedy of the commons: about 300 KB of executor context and a census of about 24 files; tokens unknown until run; no fan-out, so the shared spend is one session plus the fixed cycle, accounted in the Cost line. Drift to low performance: the order edits the hand-written floor of CLAUDE.md and the operator record, which every role reads at start; the drift observation shows each role's cold-start bytes up 4.7 to 5.5 KB over v0.3.3 with ceiling null and verdict unset, and bytes minus skillBytes is 7240 for every role, the shared component these edits can grow; the nonGoal excluding a byte or size goal leaves growth unrecorded (finding on criterion:6). Escalation: one evidence file and a list-equality script; no new command or rule, so no process provokes more process. Success to the successful: the profile shape comes from the operator's proposed profile kept in ignored intake and no alternative is weighed, which is acceptable because the operator chose it, but its provenance is unrecorded (finding on criterion:3). Shifting the burden to the intervenor: the order ends in an operator reading of their own direction record, which only the operator can do; it asks for one more reading rather than removing a recurring one. Rule beating: criterion 3 checks table rows, seven headings and resolving links, which a profile can meet with facts that go stale at the next release close (finding on criterion:3); criterion 1's verifier walkthrough is the behavioral check and is adequate. Seeking the wrong goal: the machinery-share observation is low for the last two orders (0.015 and 0.0998); a documents-only pass targets the operator's reading, which the walkthrough tests, not a proxy.
orders.removalBalance: No. The Cost line says 'Removes nothing tracked' and adds docs/evidence/WO-025/census.md plus edits across about 24 standing documents. Trimming is explicitly not a goal (nonGoal 'a byte or size goal'; criterion 6 'no document trimmed to meet one'). The profile rewrite may shorten the profile by keeping history 'only where it explains a boundary or a recovery route', but no removal is named or measured, so no removal larger than the addition is claimed.
orders.failureBehavior: Mostly degrades to the old behavior. The order is documents only and changes no code, configuration, gate input or generated surface (criterion 6's exclusions), so an abandoned pass leaves the base documents as they are and a reverted merge restores them; the census's 'unresolved facts' column records gaps rather than refusing. Two edges do not degrade cleanly. The profile is rewritten whole rather than edited, and nothing like criterion 4's digest comparison protects the profile's facts, so a rewrite that drops a boundary or recovery route the old profile carried loses it without a signal. The hand-written floor of CLAUDE.md is in the edit set without a byte-identity guard on its locked sections, so a defect there changes what every session obeys instead of leaving the old text in force (finding on criterion:6).

findings.reason: The Cost line puts 'the hand-written floor of CLAUDE.md' in the edit set, and this review's own constraint states that the clean-room floor is locked. Criterion 5 and criterion 6 guard WS-001's JSON block byte for byte and exclude scripts/, packages/, .claude/, .agents/, README.md and KIT-MANIFEST.json, but name no byte-identity check for the locked Clean Room and Secrets sections of that floor. A pass editing for usefulness, coherence or organization can reword a locked section and every criterion still passes.
findings.reopenWhen: git diff <base> HEAD -- CLAUDE.md at the reviewed tree changes any line inside the Clean Room or Secrets section, or the census records CLAUDE.md as changed without stating that those sections are byte-identical to the base.

findings.reason: Criterion 4 requires the multiset of capture digests and the multiset of dates cited in docs/operator/README.md to be equal before and after the pass. The objective asks for each standing direction once, as the rule with its date and capture, none narrated. Where the base cites one capture twice (as a rule and again in a narrated passage), the intended rewrite removes one citation and fails the criterion, so the executor is pushed to keep the narration or a duplicate citation. Comparing the sets of distinct digests and dates, with any count change accounted for in the census, would protect the same property without opposing the objective.
findings.reopenWhen: The census's before and after digest or date lists differ only in the count of an entry that still appears at least once, or the executor records keeping a duplicate citation or narrated passage solely to keep the multisets equal.

orders.systemTraps: Policy resistance: the sequence places this integration pass before five orders that each append to the documents it integrates (WO-020 adds the Studies heading and a catalog-rules rule; WO-021 to WO-024 each add a Studies entry and one more rule; WO-023 also edits events-and-state.md), so the defect the objective names, additions appended rather than integrated, returns within five orders (finding on criterion:1). Drift to low performance: no measured series attaches to target documents; the AI reference is read by coding sessions and the order rightly sets no size goal. Escalation: criterion 4 runs every command a rule document names and requires exit 0; for a serve, watch or deliberately failing example the cheapest compliance is to delete the command, so the gate reshapes the documents (finding on criterion:4). Success to the successful: the existing document set is kept as the frame, which fits a quality pass. Shifting the burden to the intervenor: the verifier's walkthrough replaces most of the operator's reading, and the operator's remaining decision is whether to hand the reference to a colleague; the burden falls. Rule beating: criterion 3's grep checks three patterns while its prose also forbids the filter row, so a stale filter-row description passes (finding on criterion:3); criterion 1's walkthrough is the behavioral check. Seeking the wrong goal: the goal is the colleague's and the coding session's reading, which the walkthrough tests; no proxy is targeted.
orders.removalBalance: No. The Cost line says 'Removes nothing tracked' and adds docs/dotln/evidence/WO-026/ records and a launchpad census. Stale references are removed from document text (criterion 3), but that is part of the edits, not a named removal of files or mechanism, and it is not larger than the addition.
orders.failureBehavior: Degrades to the old behavior. The order changes no code, route, script or configuration (nonGoals; criterion 6 limits the target diff to README.md, docs/dev-reference/, docs/ai-reference/, RELEASE-NOTES.md and docs/dotln/ and fixes package.json's dependencies), so an abandoned pass leaves the documents and the app as they are. A document that disagrees with code is corrected and a code defect found is boarded under rule 21, so a discovered defect is recorded rather than refusing the pass. The one refusing edge is criterion 4: a rule document's command that cannot exit 0 as written blocks the order unless the command is removed or rewritten (finding on criterion:4).

findings.reason: The objective asks the operator to read catalog.md as a whole with four orders' additions integrated rather than appended. The sequence then runs WO-020 to WO-024, each of which appends to the same documents by its own criterion 7: WO-020 adds catalog.md's Studies heading, a catalog-rules.md rule and a scripts.md entry; WO-021 to WO-024 each add a Studies line and one more catalog-rules.md rule; WO-023 adds pattern names to events-and-state.md. No later order carries the integration duty, so after WO-024 these files again hold five appended per-batch additions and need a second pass. Either each batch carries the integration duty or the pass's benefit for these files lasts one order; this review has no authority to reorder.
findings.reopenWhen: After WO-024 merges, catalog.md's Studies section or catalog-rules.md reads as per-batch appended paragraphs or rules, or a later planning pass proposes another quality pass over catalog.md, catalog-rules.md or events-and-state.md.

findings.reason: Criterion 4 requires every command a rule document under docs/ai-reference/ names to exit 0 when run as written. Rule documents legitimately name commands that do not terminate (serve, watch) or that demonstrate a failure, and the census records only the exit code. The cheapest compliant edit is to delete such a command, which makes the rule document less useful while the criterion passes.

WO-020 serves the sandbox outcome the goal standard names, 'a scene for authoring game AI from a toolbox mined from the works the operator reads', and is the platform step of the five batches: the study model and schema, studies:check inside check:fixtures, the study composite with the motion and timeline families, the addressable reading route and the studied marks that WO-021 to WO-024 reuse 'as it leaves them'. It therefore gates those four orders. From the order: Arrive stays the only study, hand-wired (arrive-example.ts, arrive-example-code.ts, arrive-limit-example.ts, composites/arrive-study/), each further study would be hand-wired the same way, and the catalog shows mined definitions only. Action wins because it turns one hand-wired example into a convention and removes the example, which matches the platform standard; it reopens if the later batches cannot reuse the record without changing it.
orders.systemTraps: Policy resistance: criterion 6 bans '<dl' and dotln-key-value-list across libs/features/tools/src by grep while criterion 5 holds axe at the board threshold; a text ban on the semantic element invites replacement markup that passes both while losing semantics (finding on criterion:6). Tragedy of the commons: the authoring fan-out is bounded at twelve workers, each reading two rows, with token totals recorded beside the session's and WO-014's order total and a stop decision if the sum passes it (criterion 4); this is the strongest commons accounting in the pass, though tokens are unknown until run. Drift to low performance: about 45 source files, twenty records and two commands; lazy chunks and check:bundle against WO-019's figures guard runtime drift; executor context about 230 KB. Escalation: it opens a pattern of one new catalog rule per batch (own words here; executable, analogy, embodiment and absent-material later), each checked by a one-word grep (finding on criterion:7). Success to the successful: the record contract is designed against movement concepts and then imposed on RxJS, messaging, enterprise and relational concepts; the later orders' null escape hatches and a divergent field path show the strain (WO-021's finding on criterion:3). Shifting the burden to the intervenor: criterion 8 ends design rounds only on the operator's word, and all five batches repeat it with a new pair; the burden observation shows directions of 1, 3, 6, 5 and 3 with no worsening, and the plan does not count five more rounds (finding on criterion:8). Rule beating: 'checked' with two reviewer names can be written by the authoring session itself (finding on criterion:2); criterion 1's verifier statement from the studies alone is the behavioral check. Seeking the wrong goal: 'twenty studied' is a count, but criterion 1 and the critic review make the reading the measure, and the machinery-share observation (0.015 and 0.0998 for the last two orders) shows a product focus this order keeps.
orders.removalBalance: No. It removes the hand-wired Arrive study (three files and the composites/arrive-study/ directory) and, by criterion 6, every '<dl' and dotln-key-value-list use under libs/features/tools/src. It adds a model, a schema, twenty records, a summary, loader reads, a check script with two npm commands, a composite, two visual families, model modules, a route, marks and two document sections, about 45 source files. The removal is the migration of one example; the addition is an order of magnitude larger.
orders.failureBehavior: Partly. The Arrive migration degrades safely: criterion 3 requires the migrated model's frames at the example's parameters to equal the values the base's arrive-example.spec.ts asserted, so no number changes. Studies sit below the mined definition, so the old reading is the natural fallback, but no criterion or e2e case shows that a missing, malformed or unknown study leaves the reading on the mined definition rather than an error on the new addressable route (finding on criterion:5). studies:check inside check:fixtures refuses a bad record at the gate, which is the right place to refuse. The design-comparison rounds have no end condition other than the operator's word, so an absent operator stalls the order rather than degrading to a default pick.

findings.reason: The goal standard narrates a critical path ending in a foundation that includes a legitimate client-side authentication and permission model, and asks that prerequisite or risk-reduction work name the blocked outcome it enables. The sequence places WO-008 ninth, behind two document passes, the five concept-study batches and WO-016, and none of the seven judged orders names WO-008 or any blocked outcome; their stated decisions are what to read, deepen or show next. The studies serve the sandbox outcome directly, so this is placement rather than a contradiction, no supplied vision passage id exists to cite, and goal alignment grants this review no authority to reorder.
findings.reopenWhen: A critical-path record is declared that places the authentication and permission model before the concept studies, or a later order records that it is blocked waiting on WO-008 while any of WO-020 to WO-024 is open.

findings.reason: Criterion 2 accepts a record as authored.state: 'checked' with at least two reviewers named. The reviewers are the order's own critics in the authoring fan-out, so the authoring session can write two names into a record and studies:check passes without an independent read; review.md lists findings and dispositions, but no criterion requires a named reviewer to be distinct from the record's author or to appear in fan-out.md. The same rule carries into WO-021 to WO-024.
findings.reopenWhen: Any batch's review.md or fan-out.md shows a record whose named reviewers include its authoring worker, or a reviewer named in a record who has no line in review.md or fan-out.md.

findings.reason: The study is added below the mined definition and reached through a new addressable route. The e2e cases cover the shared link, Back, the text equivalent, reduced motion, the pseudocode, the label, the count, the facet, axe and overflow, but no case opens a reading whose study is absent, malformed or names a missing model, or a reading link with an unknown id. Without one, a failed study load may replace the mined definition with an error, refusing where it should degrade to the old reading.
findings.reopenWhen: Opening the reading route for a catalog row with no study, with an unknown study id, or with a study whose visual.model fails to load shows an error or an empty page instead of the mined definition.

findings.reason: Criterion 6 bans every '<dl' and dotln-key-value-list under libs/features/tools/src by grep; the reason is not in the subject. A description list is the semantic element for name and value groups such as a reference's title, url, accessed and supports. A text ban lets replacement markup with no programmatic association pass both the grep and axe at the board threshold, so the check can pass while the semantics it should protect are lost.
findings.reopenWhen: A study composite or family renders name and value pairs (reference fields, parameters, nearby links) in markup with no list, table or labelled-group semantics, found by a screen-reader walkthrough or an axe rule beyond the board threshold.

findings.reason: WO-020 adds a catalog-rules.md rule (own words, every reference with its claim), and each later batch adds one more: the executable rule (WO-021), the analogy rule (WO-022), the embodiment rule (WO-023) and the absent-material rule (WO-024). Each is batch-specific in origin but general in effect and is checked only by a grep for one word, so after five orders catalog-rules.md carries five appended rules whose interaction no criterion tests.

The shifting-the-burden observation records directions per order of 1, 3, 6, 5 and 3 with no worsening and corrections unavailable, so the load is not a failure, but the plan neither counts five more rounds of operator design attention nor names a default when the operator does not answer.

At run time the subject states no fallback for the shelf or the toy page. In the process, the fan-out stop rule has no degraded acceptance: stopping on budget leaves the thirteen chapters or the 25 toys short, which fails c2 or c4 instead of shipping a partial mining. The stop threshold is WO-014's recorded order total, which this subject's cost table does not show (finding).

findings.reason: The clean-room evidence for the fan-out rests on each worker's own statement that no quarantine file was read. The launchpad's read observation beside it may be 'unobserved', so the criterion can pass without any observation that the intended behaviour occurred.
findings.reopenWhen: WO-018's evidence README records any worker's read observation as 'unobserved', or a non-zero harness journal row count for the quarantine path.

findings.reason: The stop rule (stop the fan-out if the token sum passes WO-014's recorded order total) has no degraded acceptance path, because c2 requires all thirteen chapters and c4 all 25 toys; a stop refuses the order instead of shipping part of the mining. The threshold depends on a recorded WO-014 token total, and this subject's cost table carries no token figures for any order.
findings.reopenWhen: The fan-outs' token sum passes WO-014's recorded order total before thirteen chapters are mapped, or WO-014's order token total is unavailable when the fan-out starts.

findings.reason: The six new toys' tools are 'typed from the work' for sources that are not in the public domain, and the nineteen toys enter 'in full' from the run's folder. c4 checks only that each public-work tool carries a definition and a source string, and c7 limits verbatim maxims to the public text. No criterion confirms that definitions drawn from non-public works are the owner's own words, or that the Art of War translation used is in the public domain.
findings.reopenWhen: Any toys.json record or tool definition is observed carrying verbatim text from a work not in the public domain, or the recorded Art of War source is a translation still under copyright.
